heading: PREFACE
src: In many a religious gathering to which I was invited during my stay in America to give a talk for fifteen minutes and no more , (as some great doctor, the chief speaker of the meeting, was to fill up the most of the time,) I often asked the chairman (or the chairwoman) what they wouldTike to hear from me. The commonest answer I received was, “O just tell us how you were converted.” I was always at loss how to comply with such a demand, as I could not in any way tell in “fifteen minutes and no more ” the awful change that came over my soul since I was brought in contact with Christianity. The fact is, the conversion of a heathen is always a matter of wonder, if not of curiosity, to the Christian public ; and it was just natural that I too was asked to tell them some vivid accounts of how WI threw: my idols into the fire, and clung unto the Gospel.'” But mine was a more obdurate case than those of many other converts. Though moments of ecstacy and sudden spiritual illuminations were not wanting, my conversion was a slow gradual process. I was not converted in a day Long after I ceased to prostrate myself before idols, yea long after I was baptized, I lacked those beliefs in the fundamental teachings of Christianity which I now consider to be esssential in calling myself a Christian. ' Even yet UI count not myself to have apprehended”; and as I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus, I know not whether I may yet find my present position to he still heathenish. These pages are the honest confessions of the various stages of the spiritual growth I have passed through.

Will the reader receive them as the unadorned expressions of a human heart, and judge with leniency the language in which they are written, as it is not the tongue that I learned' from my mother’s lips, and the ornate literature is not the trade by which I live in this world.
zh: 在我旅居美洲期間，每每被邀請到各種宗教集會演講，卻只獲分配十五分鐘時間，不可超越——蓋有某位德高望重的大家主持集會，要佔用大部分時間——我常問主持人（或女性主持人）希望聽我談論何事。最常得到的回答是：「哦，只須告訴我們您是如何歸信的。」我對於這般要求常感無所適從，蓋我根本無法在「僅十五分鐘，不可超越」之內，訴說我自與基督教相遇以來，靈魂所經歷之可怖變化。其實，異教徒的回心，對於基督教信眾而言，總是不勝其奇的，縱非好奇之對象；是故我亦自然而然地被要求講述一些生動之事蹟，訴說我如何「將我的偶像擲入烈火，而緊緊依附於福音」。然則我之情形，較諸許多其他歸信者，乃更其頑梗。雖則狂喜之時刻與靈性豁然開悟之瞬間不乏其人，吾之回心卻乃一緩慢漸進之歷程。我並非一日之間即獲轉化。長久之後，我方才不復向偶像叩拜；更待其後許久，我始受洗；然即便在受洗之後，我對於基督教基本教義之信仰，仍付闕如——而此等信仰，吾今日視之為稱名基督徒者所必需之物。即今而日，我「尚未自以為已經得著」；我既「向著標竿直跑，要得神在基督耶穌裡從上面召我來得的獎賞」，我不知吾之現今立場是否仍帶異教之色彩。此編乃吾所歷經各階段靈性成長之誠摯告白。
讀者會否將這些看作人心未經修飾的流露，並以寬容的態度來評判這樣寫出的語言？因為這不是我從母親唇邊學得的母語，也不是我以此為生的華麗文學。
喬納單‧艾克斯，此書作者。
